- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is trending up.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days) are common; cap forecast at +3–4% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is evident in 3–5 day horizons: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early in the horizon; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per 5-day segment if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., 0.67, -0.67, 0.67), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to compensate for lag.
- When sentiment is flat (0.00 or 0.33) for 3+ days, model drifts; apply 0.5–1.0% downward bias to avoid overconfidence.
